business_problem: Autodesk needed its design-simulation service to run near-real-time analyses at launch scale without burdening engineers with infrastructure management or forcing users to wait for long-running planning simulations.
solution_summary: Autodesk built Autodesk Forma on AWS as a serverless simulation platform for architects and planners who need fast feedback in the earliest design stages. When a user starts an analysis, AWS Lambda splits the work into smaller chunks that can run in parallel, AWS Step Functions coordinates the broader workflow, and Amazon ECS handles additional end-user simulation processing. Results are then combined and returned to the user for iterative decision-making. This design allows the service to scale horizontally without manual intervention and sustain launch scenarios many times beyond normal expectations. Because the platform reacts to burst demand automatically, Autodesk reduces infrastructure management work while delivering near-real-time simulations that shorten design cycles and improve user productivity.

solution_components.name: AWS Lambda
solution_components.role: Breaks simulation work into parallel tasks and executes the serverless analysis pipeline.

solution_components.name: AWS Step Functions
solution_components.role: Coordinates the stages of Autodesk Forma's simulation workflow.

solution_components.name: Amazon ECS
solution_components.role: Handles end-user simulation processing alongside the Lambda-based architecture.

data_flow: Autodesk Forma submits analysis jobs to AWS Lambda, which splits simulations into parallel chunks; AWS Step Functions coordinates the execution, Amazon ECS handles related simulation processing, and the results are collected back into near-real-time insights for the user.
business_outcome: Autodesk supports up to 100 times expected launch traffic, reduced the need for infrastructure management, lowered compute costs, improved developer productivity, and shortened user wait time for simulation completion.
metrics: Up to 100X the expected traffic supported in load testing
architecture_clues: Uses a preparation step to split simulations into parallel chunks and a collection step to recombine results.
Worked with the AWS Lambda team on burst concurrency increases before launch.
Serverless design reacts automatically to burst demand without manual intervention.
